chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Five cannot lead the people (in prayer) in any state: the leper, the one with vitiligo, the insane, the son of adultery, and the Bedouin.

key_terms.الْأَعْرَابِيُّ: the Bedouin (often implying lack of refined manners)
key_terms.يَؤُمُّونَ: lead in prayer / serve as imam

ai.seo_question: Who are the five people who cannot lead prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes the criteria for *imamah* by linking physical and social attributes to spiritual and communal suitability, reflecting the emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and *iqamah* (presence) in worship. While some scholars interpret 'A'rabi' as denoting rough manners rather than tribal origin, the inclusion of these five categories underscores the Prophet's tradition of selecting leaders who embody both physical wholeness and social refinement. This ruling is often contextualized within the broader principle that the Imam should be a source of dignity and comfort for the congregation.

en.hubeali:
A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al Husayn Bin Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Five cannot lead the people (in Salāt) upon every state – The leper, and the one with vitiligo, and the insane, and a son of adultery (bastard), and the Bedouin’.
en.sarwar: 1. A group has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from ibn Muskan from abu Basir from who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’
Five kinds of people are not to lead other people in Salah (prayer) in all circumstances: People suffering from leprosy, insanity, one born out of wedlock and al-A‘ra’biy Arab of the desert.’”
